excerpt: Convert rapidly between 200+ standard formats (PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF).
# Convert PNG to WebP with compression $ magick input.png -quality 85 output.webp
# Resize image maintaining aspect ratio $ magick input.jpg -resize 800x600^ output.jpg

Composite: overlap one image over another.
Transform: resize, rotate, deskew, crop, flip or trim an image.
Draw: add shapes or text to an image.
Decorate: add a border or frame to an image.
Montage: juxtapose image thumbnails on an image canvas.
Special effects: blur, sharpen, threshold, or tint an image.
Transparency: render portions of an image invisible.
Image gradients: create a gradual blend of one color whose shape is horizontal, vertical, circular, or elliptical.
Generalized pixel distortion: correct for, or induce image distortions including perspective.
Complex text layout bidirectional text support and shaping.
Image identification: describe the format and attributes of an image.
Image calculator: apply a mathematical expression to an image or image channels.
Histogram equalization use adaptive histogram equalization to improve contrast in images.
Delineate image features: Canny edge detection, mean-shift, Hough lines.
Connected component labeling: uniquely label connected regions in an image.
Convex hull smallest area convex polygon containing the image foreground objects. In addition, the minimum bounding box and unrotate angle are also generated.
Discrete Fourier transform: implements the forward and inverse DFT.
Perceptual hash: maps visually identical images to the same or similar hash-- useful in image retrieval, authentication, indexing, or copy detection
Encipher or decipher an image: convert ordinary images into unintelligible gibberish and back again.
Distributed pixel cache: offload intermediate pixel storage to one or more remote servers.
certain algorithms are OpenCL-enabled to take advantage of speed-ups offered by executing in concert across heterogeneous platforms consisting of CPUs, GPUs
Multispectral imagery: support multispectral imagery up to 64 bands.
Motion picture support: read and write the common image formats used in digital film work.
Image cache: secure methods and tools to cache images, image sequences, video, audio or metadata in a local folder.
ImageMagick on the iPhone: convert, edit, or compose images on your iPhone.
As of ImageMagick version 7.1.1-16, you can choose and customize one of these security policies: Open, Limited, Secure, and Websafe.
For a Q8 non-HDRI build of ImageMagick, use these configure script options: --with-quantum-depth=8 --disable-hdri.
you can enable up to 64 channels by adding the --enable-64bit-channel-masks option to the Linux configure build script.
It is written in C and can be used on a variety of operating systems, including Linux, Windows, and macOS.
Developers can integrate ImageMagick into applications to perform tasks such as resizing, color correction, format conversion, and complex image transformations.

User recalls first using ImageMagick around 2010-2011 to write a bash script that scaled and centered thousands of images into gallery thumbnails. Fred's scripts page helped them learn the scripting interface and the task was fairly simple, though they've since forgotten every parameter.
User loves ImageMagick but is surprised it is essentially the only de facto CLI image processing tool and asks whether others exist.

Fred's ImageMagick scripts called among the most useful things found online; the commenter has used several of them across many projects. Another commenter notes the downside that the scripts are free for non-commercial use only.

Analysis of the ImageTragick RCE: the URL delegate passed user-controlled input into an improperly escaped system/wget call (`wget -q -O "%o" "https:%M"`). The commenter says this was not complex formats or buffer overflows but an obscure feature that probably shouldn't have been included.

Workaround: use policy.xml to disable the EPHEMERAL, URL, HTTPS, MVG and MSL coders. One user who only needs GIF/JPG/PNG asks how to also disable PDF, FTP and others, and where to find the full coder list.

Warning not to use ImageMagick for formats like SVG or MVG, which are processed by logic as complex as a small command-line interpreter, risking XXE vulnerabilities. Running 'convert -list delegate' shows examples of this logic.
Heroku users shared a gist workaround for applying the mitigation, since /etc is read-only there. Another user noted the Paperclip library already covered the issue before disclosure.
Commenter is surprised few people have switched from ImageMagick to GraphicsMagick, given the fork happened in 2002 and, in their view, offers significant improvements.

A SaaS uses ImageMagick on Windows but says the unsigned installer doesn't affect them. They note ImageMagick is rarely used directly by end-users and is mostly shipped inside other apps, and are surprised a Windows installer exists at all instead of only portable zips.

Criticism: the commit history shows ImageMagick is still largely a one-person band, raising succession and bandwidth concerns, and the documentation site is out of date (it still mentions a Borland compiler). Suggested alternatives: libvips and GraphicsMagick.
Ubuntu users warned that some ImageMagick security patches (e.g. USN-6393-1) are only delivered via paid Expanded Security Maintenance. The commenter recommends making your own build.

User wants to de-dupe a thousand photos, including trimmed and resized copies. They believe ImageMagick has hash-based similarity methods, but say it is far from practical use for actually finding, stacking and choosing the one image to keep.

Article shows using simple ImageMagick tool calls to make an 88x31 animated button GIF scrolling all of Moby Dick: 4.2 MB, 19 hours long. Readers praised the short one-liners. GIMP crashed about 12,000 frames into loading the resulting GIF.
